is_anopheles.evidence: The paper studies Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles coluzzii (page 1, 3, 6).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports Ace-1 G119S (page 1, 3) and Ace-1 CNV (page 1, 5, 6).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 (page 8) provides genotype counts for Ace-1 G119S in Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles coluzzii.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in the field in Accra, Ghana (page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study involving field collection, genotyping, and sequencing.

sub_country_location.evidence: Collections were made in specific suburbs of Accra, Ghana, including Dzorwulu, Madina, Labadi, and Roman Ridge (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study analyzes samples collected in 2002, 2007, 2008, 2010, and 2011 (page 3, 7).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper mentions using archived samples from previous studies (Yawson et al. 2004; Lynd et al. 2010; Essandoh et al. 2013) but reports new genotyping and sequencing data for these samples.

supplement.evidence: The required genotype counts are provided in Table 1 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the genomic signatures of selection around the Ace-1 gene in Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles coluzzii from Accra, Ghana. It confirms the strong association of the Ace-1 G119S mutation with insecticide resistance and identifies a large copy number variant (CNV) associated with the resistant allele, which complicates the detection of selective sweeps.
